standard: IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

venue: EU regulated markets (all regulated markets in the 27 member states; single IAS Regulation route, no per-member-state date)
reporting_framework_before: IFRS as adopted by the EU (consolidated statements, since 2005 under Regulation (EC) No 1606/2002)
reporting_framework_after: IFRS as adopted by the EU, including IFRS 15 - NO FRAMEWORK CHANGE (repeat adopters of the standard content only)
effective_date: Annual periods beginning on or after 2018-01-01 (mandatory); earlier application permitted
first_report_date_estimate: Interim: Q1 2018 (period ended 2018-03-31), published about 2018-04-30 for quarterly filers; annual: FY2018, published about 2019-03-31. ESTIMATE derived from the effective date, not observed.
notes: QUOTES from Reg (EU) 2016/1905: recital (2) 'In May 2014, the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) issued a new International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 15 entitled Revenue from Contracts with Customers.'; recital (3) 'In September 2015 the IASB issued an amendment to IFRS 15 that defers the effective date from 1 January 2017 to 1 January 2018.'; Article 2 'Each company shall apply the amendments referred to in Article 1(1), at the latest, as from the commencement date of its first financial year starting on or after 1 January 2018.'; Article 3 'This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.' Adopted 22 September 2016; OJ L 295, 29.10.2016, p. 19-73 (OJ reference confirmed against the European Commission IAS Regulation table of implementing acts). DERIVED: entry into force 18 November 2016 (publication + 20 days, per Article 3); that derived date is the earliest date on which the EU endorsement is legally operative, and is the candidate T-A for the EU H-A announcement window. DATE CONFLICT RECORDED: the EU recital gives only 'May 2014' for issuance; the day-level issuance date 2014-05-28 is taken from the joint IASB/FASB press release (S-33), which is the same issuance event. CONFLICT NOT RESOLVED BY SELECTION: if a study needs a different day, both readings must be carried.
first_time_vs_repeat_coexistence: NO framework-changer in the EU for IFRS 15: the EU has required IFRS for consolidated statements of listed companies since 2005, so IFRS 15 is a content change for every EU filer. There is no first-time/repeat contrast inside the EU for this standard. The only within-EU heterogeneity is non-IFRS-specific (see EV-002 for the IFRS 9 insurance deferral).

notes: QUOTES from Reg (EU) 2016/2067: recital (2) 'On 24 July 2014, the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) published International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 9 Financial Instruments.'; Article 2 'Each company shall apply the amendments referred to in Article 1(1), at the latest, as from the commencement date of its first financial year starting on or after 1 January 2018.'; recital (5) 'while endorsing IFRS 9, the need for an optional deferral of its application for the insurance sector is recognised ... the Commission intends to give an option to the insurance sector not to apply IFRS 9 for a limited period of time.' DERIVED: entry into force 19 December 2016 (publication + 20 days). DATE CONFLICT RECORDED: the EU recital gives the issuance date as 24 July 2014; the date commonly cited elsewhere is 25 July 2014, and the IFRS Foundation's own standard-history page for IFRS 9 states only 'In July 2014 the Board issued IFRS 9'. first_time_vs_repeat_coexistence: NO framework-changer in the EU for IFRS 9. Documented WITHIN-EU HETEROGENEITY IN APPLICATION DATE: the insurance sector received a temporary exemption from IFRS 9, so EU insurers (a listed, cross-jurisdiction sub-population) applied IFRS 9 later than the rest of the EU market. That is a date heterogeneity inside one jurisdiction and one standard, not a framework change, and it must be handled as a pre-registered carve-out rather than as a treatment arm.

notes: PARTIAL VERIFICATION, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW IN THIS FILE FOR THE DESIGN. The UK is the only jurisdiction inside the frozen universe where a documented within-jurisdiction first-time/repeat-style split for IFRS 15 is known to exist: early application of IFRS 15 for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2015, against mandatory application for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2016. That creates two different first-report dates inside one jurisdiction, which is exactly what the frozen design's treatment/control contrast needs and what the EU does not provide. first_time_vs_repeat_coexistence: YES (documented, but on the standard-content reading, not the framework-change reading): UK early adopters of IFRS 15 for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2015 coexist with mandatory adopters for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2016, inside one jurisdiction and one market. Caveat that must carry into any v1.1: the canonical dossier rejects this contrast as an IDENTIFICATION (V-009 Cycle-56, item 3) because the early arm is voluntary, self-selected, mechanically correlated with the firm-level state the design conditions on, small in number, and publishes its first IFRS 15 statements together with their effect, so the diffusion clock has no window to run. It is recorded here as an existing within-jurisdiction split, not as a validated design.
